The EU acknowledges that these challenges could lead to a backlash against green policies in rural areas as right-wing and populist parties gain ground.

articles.title: AI-Guided Cruise Missiles: 'Special mission warhead': North Korea tests AI-guided cruise missiles, ballistic rockets near South Korea | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: North Korea conducted a series of missile tests, including tactical ballistic missiles, artillery rockets, and AI-guided cruise missiles, near South Korea. The tests were designed to assess the power of a "special mission warhead" mounted on the missiles and the accuracy of the AI-guided cruise missiles.  Kim Jong Un, leader of North Korea, stated that these weapons will be deployed near the border with South Korea, equipped with precision navigation and AI-guided control capable of striking targets at 100 km (62 miles).

articles.title: Centre fears ‘divergence of views’ among High Courts on new transgender law; asks SC to transfer cases to itself - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre urged the Supreme Court to transfer petitions challenging the constitutionality of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026 from four High Courts to itself. Solicitor General Tishar Mehta argued that High Courts may pre-empt the apex court by taking up the cases before them and passing orders. The petitions, led by activists like Laxminarayan Tripathi, criticize the Act for removing the right to self-identity and requiring a medical board's recommendation for gender recognition.

articles.title: Israel claims it killed new Hamas armed wing chief in Gaza strike - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Israel announced the killing of Mohammed Odeh, the new head of Hamas's armed wing in Gaza, in a strike on Tuesday.  Israel Defense Minister Israel Katz and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Odeh was responsible for the October 7th massacre and had been appointed to succeed Ezzedine al-Haddad, who was killed by an Israeli strike earlier this month. The IDF and Shin Bet were praised for their execution of the operation.

articles.title: Amanda Rishworth says jobseekers will no longer be forced to submit ‘endless’ pointless job applications | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Amanda Rishworth, the employment minister, announced a new three-stream system for the employment services sector, aiming to address concerns about its current "one-size fits all" approach. The system will differentiate between jobseekers based on their skills and work readiness, offering digital resources for those ready to work, targeted support for skill building, and intensive services for complex cases. While welcoming changes to mutual obligations activities, advocacy groups like Acoss and the Community and Public Sector Union called for a complete overhaul of the privatized model, arguing it has failed jobseekers and the government.

articles.title: Longview explosion: one killed and nine missing after blast at paper mill
articles.rephrased_article: A chemical explosion at a Nippon Dynawave Packaging paper mill in Longview, Washington, resulted in one fatality and nine missing individuals. The explosion occurred due to a ruptured tank containing white liquor, a highly corrosive chemical used in the paper-making process.  The incident injured nine people, including eight employees and one firefighter, with injuries ranging from minor to critical. Washington Governor Bob Ferguson expressed condolences for the victims and first responders.  Cowlitz Fire and Rescue Chief Scott Goldstein stated that the scene remains stable but is undergoing recovery efforts.

articles.title: Adani Power surpasses Infosys in market capitalisation after 126% rally in one year - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Adani Power's stock surged to become India's 11th most valued company, driven by soaring power demand fueled by the intense El Niño year and heatwave conditions.  The surge comes as India grapples with record-breaking temperatures, placing it among the world's hottest cities. Infosys, meanwhile, saw its share price decline due to concerns about the impact of AI advancements on the software-as-a-service market.

articles.title: Taiwan’s economy is booming thanks to AI. Not everyone sees the benefits | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Taiwan's economy is experiencing rapid growth due to its semiconductor industry, which powers leading AI models.  However, this boom has raised concerns about wealth inequality and the uneven distribution of benefits. While the stock market has seen significant gains, many Taiwanese workers in non-tech sectors are facing rising costs for housing and living expenses. The Central Bank Governor Yang Chin-lung has sounded the alarm about an "K-shaped economy," where certain sectors grow rapidly while others stagnate.  Some argue that Taiwan's economic model is becoming too reliant on a single industry, leaving other sectors behind.

articles.title: FM Dar assures UN chief of Pakistan's 'continued engagement and dialogue' to restore peace in region - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, met with António Guterres, the UN Secretary-General, in New York to discuss regional developments.  Dar praised Guterres' commitment to multilateralism and highlighted Pakistan's successful mediation efforts in the US-Iran war. He also discussed South Asia, specifically India's provocative statements and unilateral actions regarding the Indus Water Treaty, as well as concerns over Afghanistan's stability and terrorism emanating from its soil. Dar emphasized the importance of a peaceful and stable Afghanistan for regional security and reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to international law and UN principles.  He also addressed Palestine and the need for a two-state solution.

articles.title: Australian BTS fans blast Ticketmaster’s ‘predatory’ tactic of hiding price until tickets go on sale | BTS | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ticketmaster Australia has faced criticism from BTS Army, the group's fanbase, for its lack of pricing information and seating maps ahead of presale tickets for upcoming concerts in Melbourne and Sydney. The Consumer Policy Research Centre (CPRC) called the strategy "manipulative" and "deeply unfair," while fans on social media expressed concerns about being pressured into high-priced purchases under a time limit.  The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) stated that businesses are not required to disclose prices in advance, but will investigate complaints of misleading pricing practices.

articles.title: Texas Attorney General Paxton routs veteran incumbent Cornyn in US Senate primary
articles.rephrased_article: Ken Paxton, the Texas Attorney General, defeated incumbent Senator John Cornyn in a Republican primary runoff election. This stunning defeat for the veteran senator marks a significant shift in Texas politics and sets up a closely watched general election contest between Paxton and Democratic candidate James Talarico.  Paxton's victory, fueled by his populist appeal and Trump's endorsement, could potentially impact the balance of power in the US Senate during Donald Trump's final two years in office.  The outcome also highlights the influence of Trump's base in Texas, where voters appear to favor firebrand conservative candidates over more establishment figures.

articles.title: DRC flight suspension and Uganda border curbs isolate Ebola-hit Bunia | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has suspended all flights to and from Bunia, capital of Ituri province, in an attempt to contain an ongoing Ebola outbreak.  The Ministry of Transport and Communications implemented this measure to prevent cross-border spread of the virus.  Uganda, a major trade partner for Bunia, has also imposed travel restrictions on DRC citizens, further isolating the city's economy. Businesses are struggling with disruptions to supply chains and reduced tourism due to the closures. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has pledged over $500 million in support for the response to the outbreak.

articles.title: Dissident detained in South Korea after fleeing China in rubber boat | China | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 68-year-old Chinese dissident, Dong Guangping, was apprehended by South Korean coast guard after attempting to flee China in a rubber boat.  He had previously attempted to escape multiple times, including being deported back to China from Thailand and Vietnam. Zang Xihong, a Chinese dissident in Canada, has been in contact with Dong since 2015 and confirmed his determination to leave China despite previous failures.  The distance between Weifang, China, and Taean, South Korea, is over 300km.

articles.title: First Ghanaians set to be repatriated from South Africa over anti-immigrant protests
articles.rephrased_article: Ghanaian authorities are repatriating the first group of 800 citizens registered to leave South Africa, following a wave of anti-immigrant protests. The repatriation effort began Wednesday morning with dozens of buses chartered by the Ghanaian embassy dropping off passengers at Johannesburg's OR Tambo airport.  The remaining registered citizens will be screened and depart later, according to Ghanaian High Commissioner Benjamin Quashie. March and March, a citizen-led movement for immigration reform, has organized protests demanding illegal immigrants leave the country by June 30th. The protests have sparked concerns about potential violence as some fear the deadline could lead to xenophobic attacks.

articles.title: Veteran Texas congressman Al Green beaten in Democratic primary runoff | Texas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Christian Menefee, a freshman Democratic US representative, defeated veteran congressman Al Green in a runoff election. The victory was attributed to Republican gerrymandering that eliminated Green's reliably Democratic ninth district.  Donald Trump had urged the state legislature to protect the GOP’s congressional majority, and Green has been a vocal critic of the Trump administration.

articles.title: What Tamil Nadu CM Vijay really needs to see at Fort St. George - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the newly elected Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, visited Fort St. George last week but did not see all of its historical sites. The Fort is facing issues with poor general upkeep, including piles of trash and a neglected moat. These problems are visible throughout the precinct, highlighting the need for improvement to preserve this historic enclave.

articles.title: New airline South Air operates trial flight to Gwadar - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: South Air, a private airline, launched its first trial flight service from Karachi to Gwadar, marking a significant step towards improved air travel facilities in the coastal region. The flight successfully landed at the New Gwadar International Airport on Tuesday afternoon, with the operationalization of the airport under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) project expected to facilitate smoother movement of passengers and cargo.  The new air service is anticipated to reduce travel time between Gwadar, Karachi, Quetta, and other cities while boosting trade, tourism, and development activities across the Makran division.

articles.title: Iran war live: Israel kills 31 in Lebanon; Tehran blasts US truce violation | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel intensified its attacks in southern Lebanon, killing 31 people and injuring 40 others on Tuesday. Israeli forces issued forced displacement orders for towns and villages in the region.  The Lebanese Health Ministry reports that since March 2nd, Israeli attacks have killed 3,213 people and injured 9,737.

articles.title: Bangladesh measles cases: Hundreds of children die within months
articles.rephrased_article: Over 500 children have died in Bangladesh from measles since March, according to the country's health ministry.  UNICEF reports that hospitals are overwhelmed and struggling to isolate measles patients due to a lack of resources. Sheikh Hassina, Bangladesh's long-term ruler, fled the country in 2024, leading to delays in vaccine procurement during an interim government period. The Bangladesh Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched an emergency vaccination campaign at the start of April, which has helped slow the spread but it will take time for the impact to be felt nationwide.

articles.title: Islamabad plans oil reserves, storage push - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's energy ministry is proposing to build strategic petroleum reserves and commercial storage through bonded terminals, refineries, and oil marketing companies to increase its energy security. The government plans to cut reliance on imports from the Strait of Hormuz by boosting domestic production and refining capacity.  The proposed framework, shared with international oil producers and trading firms, aims to create commercial inventories that could support domestic supply during emergencies.

articles.title: Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro meets with Trump amid troubled presidential bid | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, met with US President Donald Trump at the White House.  Bolsonaro is seeking to bolster his image amid a scandal that threatens his presidential campaign in Brazil. The meeting comes after a report revealed he sought funds from a disgraced banker for a film about his father. Recent polls suggest the scandal has set back his campaign, with Lula retaking the lead.

articles.title: Three killed in Israeli strike on Gaza City, medics and witnesses say
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli forces carried out a major air strike on a residential building in Gaza City, killing at least three Palestinians and injuring dozens more. The attack targeted Mohammed Odeh, the commander of Hamas's armed wing, according to Israel's Prime Minister's office.  Rescue teams struggled to reach the upper floors due to the scale of the damage and congestion. This latest strike comes despite a ceasefire being in place since October 10th, with both Hamas and Israel accusing each other of breaching the agreement. The attack follows a series of deadly Israeli strikes on Gaza, raising concerns about the fragile peace process.

articles.title: Storied New York food co-op votes to boycott Israeli products after contentious campaign | New York | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Members of the Park Slope Food Coop in Brooklyn voted to boycott approximately a dozen products from Israel and Israeli settlements in occupied Palestine, marking the culmination of years of debate over the conflict.  Sixty-seven percent of participants supported the boycott, which was led by Park Slope Food Coop Members in Solidarity with Palestine and endorsed by several advocacy groups, including Jewish ones. The decision has drawn attention beyond the co-op, with some members like Dan Goldman and Brad Lander, both Democrats running for congressional office, weighing in on the issue.  The debate has also been marked by tensions between pro-boycott advocates and anti-boycott members, leading to confrontations and accusations of antisemitism and racism.

articles.title: Sensex falls 70 points, Nifty below 23,900 as US-Iran tensions simmer - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex opened lower on Wednesday, declining around 70 points to reach near 75,940. The Nifty 50 also fell over 33 points, opening at 23,880.  Despite this, the India VIX dropped more than 3%. While some stocks like Sun Pharma and ITC saw gains, others such as HDFC Bank, Infosys, and Axis Bank experienced losses. Analysts suggest that the Indian market is being weighed down by foreign institutional investor (FII) selling due to global markets' bull rally.  However, analysts also highlight positive developments from Q4 results, including strong midcap performance and profit growth outpacing revenue growth.

articles.title: Iran vows not to let aggression go unanswered after US violates truce - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iran accused the United States of violating a ceasefire by targeting its missile sites and mine-laying boats. The US responded with strikes, claiming they were self-defense to protect troops from Iranian threats.  Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, stated that a deal to end the conflict could be reached within days. However, he emphasized the importance of reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has threatened retaliation and warned against any further US or Israeli air strikes on its territory. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump is holding a cabinet meeting at Camp David as talks between Iran and the US approach a critical point.

articles.title: Group of women and children with alleged ISIL ties returns to Australia | ISIL/ISIS News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Australian Federal Police have not made any arrests but are continuing investigations into a group of 19 women and children who returned to Australia from a Syrian refugee camp. The group, which arrived in Sydney and Melbourne on Tuesday, has sparked anger in some sections of Australian society due to alleged links to ISIL.  The government maintains it did not assist the group's return and emphasized that anyone found to have engaged in criminal activity will be prosecuted.

articles.title: Russia 'relentlessly targeting' critical infrastructure, democracy - GCHQ
articles.rephrased_article: The UK's GCHQ Director, Anne Keast-Butler, will warn of the "relentless targeting" by Russia of critical infrastructure and democracy in her inaugural public speech.  Keast-Butler highlighted Russia's involvement in espionage plots, cyber attacks, and attempts to undermine public trust. She emphasized GCHQ's efforts to counter these threats alongside intelligence and defense partners. The agency also addressed the growing influence of China, urging collaboration with industry, academia, and the public to stay ahead in the race for technological advancements.

articles.title: Paul Keating urges Labor to stick with capital gains tax overhaul and avoid exemptions that would hurt economy | Tax | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Paul Keating urged Labor to maintain its stance on controversial capital gains tax changes, warning that exempting commercial assets would further distort the economy.  The architect of major economic reforms in the 1980s and 90s, Keating argued that correcting the balance between capital and labor taxation should be a priority. The treasurer, Jim Chalmers, has also expressed concerns about creating new distortions in the tax system. However, investors and entrepreneurs are fiercely opposed to the government's plans, warning they will hinder investment and risk-taking.  The legislation is expected to include changes to negative gearing rules, a $1,000 standard tax deduction, and a new $250-a-year tax offset for workers.

articles.title: ED raids former Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan’s houses in CMRL pay-off case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted raids on the homes of former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and his family, along with other locations across the state, in connection with an investigation into alleged political payoffs. The ED's action followed a High Court order allowing them to investigate Exalogic, a firm owned by Vijayan's daughter, T. Veena, which allegedly received monthly retainers from Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) during the 2017-2021 period without providing tangible services. The ED is investigating whether these payments constituted money laundering.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Raids on a former CM's home raise concerns about potential abuse of power.

articles.title: Top 10 countries with fastest billionaire growth by 2031: Saudi Arabia, Poland and Sweden top the global wealth race | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: World of Statistics (formerly Twitter) predicts a significant rise in billionaire populations globally over the next few years, with notable shifts occurring outside traditional Western economic centers. Saudi Arabia, driven by diversification away from oil dependence, stands out for its rapid growth, while Poland experiences acceleration fueled by manufacturing strength and technology outsourcing. Sweden, Australia, Denmark, Japan, Mexico, and the Philippines also show varying degrees of growth, with factors like technology, green industries, and services-based expansion playing key roles.  These trends suggest a more fragmented and dynamic wealth landscape than previously anticipated.

articles.title: Trump-backed Paxton topples Senator Cornyn in Texas primary run-off | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ken Paxton, Texas Attorney General, defeated John Cornyn in the Republican primary run-off for US Senate, securing a November election that could decide control of the chamber.  Paxton's victory was fueled by President Donald Trump's endorsement and marked a significant blow to the party establishment. The outcome is likely to make Paxton the Democrats' top target in November as he faces off against Democratic state Representative James Talarico.

articles.title: Can the EU find a Russia whisperer to mediate an end to the war in Ukraine?
articles.rephrased_article: The EU is considering re-engaging with Russia to mediate an end to the war in Ukraine.  Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha has suggested a new format for talks, involving more active participation from the European side. While former German chancellor Angela Merkel and ex-Prime Minister of Italy Mario Draghi are rumored as potential envoys, no names have been confirmed. Russia is currently escalating its aggression against Ukraine, threatening "systematic strikes" on the country. The EU aims to ensure any deal reached would be beneficial for both Ukraine and European security.  However, serious negotiations remain uncertain due to Russia's unwillingness to engage with the EU or US.

articles.title: ‘Makes no sense’: experts doubt pause in US arms sale to Taiwan is due to Iran war | Taiwan | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Experts have stated that the Trump administration's war against Iran should not impact arms sales to Taiwan, as a $14 billion package is unlikely to be delivered for several years.  The US acting navy secretary, Hung Cao, suggested a pause in the delivery of weapons due to the Iran conflict, but analysts argue this justification makes no sense and that any connection between events in Iran and arms sales to Taiwan is "very very low." The US-Taiwan Business Council president, Rupert Hammond-Chambers, believes the delay would not affect future arms deals.

articles.title: Quad FMs announce maritime, energy initiatives amidst Hormuz chokehold, tense South China Sea - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Quad foreign ministers met in New Delhi on May 26, 2026, to address challenges in the Indo-Pacific region.  The meeting resulted in initiatives focused on maritime security and energy resilience, including the launch of the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration initiative and the expansion of the Indo-Pacific Maritime Domain Awareness initiative. The group also reaffirmed its commitment to upholding international law and peaceful resolution of disputes. S. Jaishankar (India), Marco Rubio (United States), Toshimitsu Motegi (Japan), and Penny Wong (Australia) emphasized the importance of "safe maritime commerce" and condemned attacks on commercial shipping vessels.  The meeting also saw the announcement of the Quad Ports of the Future Partnership, a pilot project for port infrastructure in Fiji.

articles.title: Raichur MP raises concern over proposed Information Technology Act amendments - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: G. Kumar Naik, a member of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communication and Information Technology, has urged Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, to reconsider certain provisions in the draft Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Second Amendment Rules 2026.  Naik expressed concerns that the proposed amendments could impact democratic participation, free expression, and Constitutional safeguards by expanding the scope of Part III of the rules and enabling direct Ministry referrals to an Inter-Departmental Committee without a complaint from an aggrieved party. He also raised objections to linking intermediary safe harbor protections under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act 2000 to compliance with government advisories, clarifications, and standard operating procedures.  Naik emphasized the importance of balancing platform accountability and online safety with Constitutional guarantees of free expression and independent oversight in India's evolving digital governance framework.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh launches initiative to clear water hyacinth and revive water bodies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Andhra Pradesh government launched a mission to revitalize water bodies and generate income for women through innovative waste management practices.  S. Suresh Kumar, Principal Secretary of the Municipal Administration and Urban Development (MA&UD) department, stated that the initiative will address the spread of invasive water hyacinth by removing it from identified water bodies while also preventing untreated sewage from entering them. The program aims to convert harvested biomass into value-added products like organic compost and handicrafts, creating new income opportunities for women's self-help groups.

articles.title: Cyberabad Police Commissioner inspects IIIT Junction flyover and underpass works in Gachibowli - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cyberabad Police Commissioner M. Ramesh inspected ongoing road development and traffic infrastructure works at the IIIT Junction in Gachibowli, Hyderabad.  During the inspection, Ramesh reviewed progress on multi-level flyovers and underpasses being constructed to alleviate congestion in the IT corridor. He directed officials to implement traffic diversions, develop alternative routes, install signage and lighting, and deploy personnel for traffic regulation. The project aims to be completed within the stipulated timeframe while prioritizing public safety.

articles.title: Extreme heatwave hits A.P. as Vijayawada north soars to 47.3°C - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh is experiencing a prolonged heatwave with temperatures exceeding 47°C in many areas. The Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES) reported that extreme heat has affected 15 mandals, while the AP State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) recorded heatwaves in 116 mandals across 14 districts.  India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued orange alerts for central Andhra Pradesh until May 29th and warned of severe heatwave conditions on May 27th in several districts, including Polavaram, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, West Godavari, and Eluru.

articles.title: India-U.S. and Quad frameworks on critical minerals take shape amid Chinese curbs - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India and the United States finalized a framework agreement on critical minerals during the 11th Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, aiming to deepen cooperation across mining, processing, recycling, and related investments. This follows growing concerns over China's export controls on rare earth minerals and strategic metals. The agreement, built upon continued engagements between the two countries, seeks to mobilize around $20 billion in support for stable supply chains and strengthen resilient and diversified supply chains within Quad partner countries, including Australia, Japan, and the United States.  The initiatives are expected to address global shortages of critical metals exacerbated by China's export controls.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death: Madhya Pradesh DGP defends Bhopal Police as CBI takes over case, launches probe - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Madhya Pradesh Director General of Police (DGP) Kailash Makwana stated that the Bhopal Police followed established procedures in the Twisha Sharma death case, which was subsequently taken over by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).  The family has alleged institutional bias and procedural lapses by local police, including accusations against retired district judge Giribala Singh, who is an accused in the dowry death and harassment case. The CBI team visited Ms. Singh's residence and questioned her while also meeting with the victim’s family members. The High Court will hear petitions challenging Ms. Singh’s anticipatory bail on May 27th.

articles.title: Jury seated as US trial of Catholic priest accused of sexual assault begins | Texas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A jury of eight women and four men was selected for the criminal trial of Anthony Odiong, a Roman Catholic priest, who is charged with sexually assaulting three women in Waco, Texas.  Odiong faces five counts of first-degree sexual assault and two counts of second-degree sexual assault. The charges stem from allegations made by several women who accused him of exploiting their emotional dependency for sexual purposes while he was ministering in Texas and Louisiana. Prosecutors will present evidence that Odiong violated the Catholic promise of celibacy, fathered a child with a congregant, and engaged in inappropriate financial control over his accusers.  Odiong's lawyers argue that the state waited too long to file charges against him, introducing hearsay testimony about the number of accusers. The trial is expected to last into next week.

articles.title: Fuel shortage hits pumps amid panic buying; OMCs call for calm, say supply is steady - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Farmers across several states in India are facing fuel shortages due to the recent hike in fuel prices.  The Centre has implemented price hikes to mitigate losses for its oil marketing companies (OMCs), but this has led to supply disruptions and long queues at petrol stations.  In Maharashtra, farmers are struggling to procure diesel for their tractors, while in Punjab, the Punjab Petrol Pump Dealers Association reports short supplies of both petrol and diesel. The situation is impacting agricultural activities and transportation, with some fuel stations even running dry.  The Petroleum Ministry has assured the public that there is no shortage of fuel but urged people to avoid panic buying.

articles.title: Clarence B Jones, who helped MLK write ‘I have a dream’ speech, dies at 95 | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Clarence B Jones, a former speechwriter and confidante of Martin Luther King Jr., died at the age of 95 on Friday.  Jones was heavily involved in key moments of the civil rights movement, including smuggling pages of King's "Letter from Birmingham jail" out of his cell and writing many up until King’s assassination in 1968. He helped craft King’s “Beyond Vietnam: a time to break silence” address given at Riverside church in New York, which was considered a hallmark speech for King’s condemnation of the Vietnam war. Jones went on to become a scholar-in-residence at Stanford University's Martin Luther King Jr Research and Education Institute and taught law students at the University of San Francisco.  He received the nation’s highest civilian award, the presidential medal of freedom, from Joe Biden in 2023.

articles.title: UFC arena under construction on White House lawn to mark Trump’s 80th birthday | West Coast | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump is hosting a UFC fight on the White House lawn next month to celebrate the US's 250th anniversary and his 80th birthday. The event, scheduled for June 14th, will feature two title fights: a lightweight championship bout between Ilia Topuria and Justin Gaethje, and an interim heavyweight title fight between Alex Pereira and Ciryl Gane.  Construction is underway on the temporary arena, which will include a stage, a red, white and blue arch, and thousands of seats.

articles.title: SOCIETY: DANCES WITH THE GORILLA - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The viral "gorilla" trend has taken over private events and celebrations in Pakistan, blurring the lines between spectacle and parody.  While some see it as a novelty, others view it as an extension of internet trends like exaggerated dance performances or masked characters. The gorilla's popularity stems from its ability to disrupt established rituals while remaining playful and easily replicated. It taps into a long-standing fascination with non-human figures in South Asian culture, offering a portable form of absurdity that demands little interpretation but relies on the erasure of the performer's human identity.  The gorilla's success highlights how internet trends are increasingly shaping celebration, creating new rituals and blurring the boundaries between spectacle and reality.

articles.title: Trump urges Texas Republicans to vote for Ken Paxton as four-term senator John Cornyn fights to hold seat – live | Texas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Texas voters head to the polls for a runoff election in which Attorney General Ken Paxton faces incumbent Senator John Cornyn.  Trump endorsed Paxton, who is seeking to become the next US senator from Texas. The White House announced plans to host a UFC fight on its grounds to mark the United States's 250th anniversary and Donald Trump's 80th birthday. NASA revealed ambitious plans for three uncrewed lunar missions this year.  Iran accused the United States of violating a ceasefire after conducting overnight strikes, while SpaceX was awarded a $2.29 billion contract to build a satellite communications network. The US Space Force also announced a new initiative to control information flow within the government.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh emerges as a pioneer in AI-driven healthcare innovations, says Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Minister for Health, Medical Education, and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav praised the use of AI in medical diagnostics, highlighting its accuracy, speed, and affordability.  The National Health Authority and Ratan Tata Innovation Hub collaborated on the MedTech Innovation Challenge, which saw 297 applications from researchers and innovators evaluated across four categories. Winners were awarded cash prizes and certificates for their AI-powered diagnostic tests, portable point-of-care testing devices, smart monitoring and wearable technology, and remote care solutions.

articles.title: Europe sizzles under record May heatwave; 7 die in France - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Western Europe experienced record-breaking temperatures during a heatwave, with France, Britain, and Spain all reporting high temperatures exceeding normal May averages.  At least seven people died in France due to the extreme weather conditions, including drownings in bodies of water. The Met Office in Britain attributed the record-breaking temperatures to climate change, while scientists warned that human-driven climate change is intensifying heatwaves and other extreme weather events across Europe.

articles.title: NA panel takes govt to task over budget preparation, reforms - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A parliamentary committee in Pakistan expressed concern over the government's failure to circulate and publish the Budget Strategy Paper by May 10th, as well as its continued reliance on indirect taxes and petroleum levy. Syed Naveed Qamar, former finance minister of the PPP, criticized the lack of progress on structural reforms and highlighted the growing burden of circular debt in the energy sector.  Dr Ali Salman, a private economist representing the UNDP, warned that inflation could undermine economic growth due to rising prices for essential goods. The committee also expressed concern about Pakistan's dependence on foreign imports and the vulnerability of the economy to regional geopolitical instability.

articles.title: Russia is targeting UK’s infrastructure and democracy, GCHQ head to say | GCHQ | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: GCHQ head Anne Keast-Butler will warn that the UK is facing a "new era of radical uncertainty" due to relentless cyberattacks from Russia and China.  Keast-Butler highlighted the growing sophistication of China's intelligence capabilities, particularly in AI, while emphasizing the urgent need for the UK to stay ahead. The spy chief will also address the increasing use of information and technology as weapons by adversaries like Russia, citing recent incidents involving firebombs placed in DHL parcels.  The UK government has responded with sanctions targeting Russian-linked cryptocurrency platforms and financial networks, aiming to disrupt their operations and undermine Russia's war economy.

articles.title: US senator says he was pepper-sprayed by federal agents during protest at ICE facility | ICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Senator Andy Kim and Governor Mikie Sherrill, both Democrats, joined protests outside an immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey, where they witnessed clashes with federal agents.  Kim reported being pepper-sprayed by ICE officials while attempting to de-escalate a situation involving protesters and agents. Demonstrators allege detainees have been denied food, medical care, and air conditioning at the facility, prompting a hunger strike and work stoppage. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin denied claims of a hunger strike, stating that conditions are not sub-prime.  The protests come amid stalled efforts to pass a funding measure for ICE and border patrol, with Senate Republicans blocking the bill due to disagreements over Trump's plans for a White House ballroom and a "anti-weaponization" fund.

articles.title: Capital Hospital performs high-risk cardiac surgery on dialysis patient in Vijayawada - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Capital Hospitals in the city successfully performed a high-risk cardiac surgery on a 34-year-old woman with end-stage kidney disease and severe heart valve dysfunction. The patient, who was dependent on dialysis twice a week, had been diagnosed with Mitral Valve Regurgitation, making transplantation dangerous without first correcting the cardiac problem. A multidisciplinary team performed a Mitral Valve Replacement surgery followed by monitoring before discharge.

articles.title: Diplomacy, new war technology vital to deter India, say experts - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Academicians, diplomats, military and war experts gathered at the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad (ISSI) to discuss the importance of diplomacy in maintaining strategic stability in South Asia. Professor Dr Zafar Nawaz Jaspal, Vice Chancellor of Quaid-e-Azam University, emphasized the need for sustained dialogue between India and Pakistan for regional peace, noting that the current deadlock has hindered confidence-building measures and arms control.  Dr Rizwana Abbasi, a professor at NUML's Department of International Relations, highlighted how India's evolving military posture and new technologies are increasing regional instability. Air Commodore (Retd.) Khalid Banuri discussed the changing character of war with the emergence of AI, hypersonic missiles, and space-based systems, emphasizing the need for human oversight in decision-making processes.  **Maj. Gen. Ausaf Ali (Retd.

articles.title: Israel is no longer ‘shooting and crying’ | Crimes Against Humanity | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The recent revelations about the brutal torture of Palestinian prisoners in Israeli jails, including rape and sexual violence, have exposed a disturbing reality of Palestinian life under Israeli occupation.  Israeli guards are documented committing these acts while laughing, raising concerns about the normalization of such behavior within society. This gleeful violence is not unique to this instance but has been a trend since the 2010s, with Israelis celebrating their soldiers' efficiency in killing Palestinians and viewing such actions as rewarding.  The article argues that this glee stems from a deeply ingrained settler colonial worldview that dehumanizes Palestinians and associates violence with rewards, ultimately leading to a society that celebrates and embraces such atrocities.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article reports systematic torture and abuse by Israeli guards, raising serious human rights concerns.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Nelson Mandela: “If you talk to a man in a language he understands, that goes to his head. If you talk to him in his language, that goes to his heart.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nelson Mandela's quote, "If you talk to a man in a language he understands, that goes to his head. If you talk to him in his language, that goes to his heart," explores the distinction between understanding information and feeling connected emotionally through shared language or cultural experiences. The quote highlights how communication transcends mere linguistic exchange and emphasizes the importance of recognizing another person's unique perspective and background. This resonates with people because it speaks to a fundamental human need for connection and recognition.

articles.title: North Korea fired projectiles, including short-range ballistic missile, Seoul says - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: North Korea fired several projectiles, including at least one short-range ballistic missile, toward waters off its west coast on Tuesday. The South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff said the missiles flew about 80 kilometers and are North Korea's first known launch since April 19th.  South Korea’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson urged North Korea to respond to peace overtures and reduce tensions, while Seoul maintained its goal of complete denuclearization.

articles.title: Albert Manifold ousted as BP chair over governance and conduct concerns | Oil and Gas News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: BP chairman Albert Manifold has been ousted after only eight months on the job due to "serious concerns" regarding governance standards, oversight, and conduct. The board made the decision unanimously, with interim chair Ian Tyler taking over immediately.  This follows a series of leadership changes at the oil and gas giant, including the abrupt departure of CEO Murray Auchincloss and former CEO Bernard Looney. BP's stock is down in both US and UK markets following the announcement.

articles.title: ‘Just take it away’: Mother of teen who died after alleged TikTok challenge urges UK govt to ban social media - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ellen Roome, whose 14-year-old son Jools Sweeney died in 2022 after attempting a dangerous online challenge, is urging the UK government to take immediate action on restricting children's access to social media.  She and other bereaved parents will meet with Prime Minister Keir Starmer on Tuesday as a national consultation on a possible social media ban for under-16s nears its conclusion.  Wes Streeting, former UK health secretary, has also called for stricter regulation of social media platforms, comparing them to the tobacco industry and highlighting the potential harm caused by excessive use among children. TikTok is facing legal action in the US from families who lost children due to a dangerous online challenge, with Roome calling for access to platform data to understand what content their children were exposed to.

articles.title: Reform UK civil service plan ‘would sack more planning officers than exist’ | Reform UK | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Reform UK, led by MP Danny Kruger, has proposed a plan to cut the size of the civil service by 13%, resulting in job losses for planning officers and psychologists. The plan aims to save over £5 billion annually by reducing roles in areas like communications, human resources, and security. Mike Wood, shadow Cabinet Office minister, criticized the plan as unrealistic and harmful, arguing it would weaken critical services like prison safety and cybersecurity.

articles.title: Banners warn of ‘property seizure’ for cattle slaughter in Karnataka - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Banners put up by Hassan City Corporation and the district administration in certain areas of Hassan city, Karnataka, ahead of Bakrid, sparked controversy after they threatened to seize property for cattle slaughter violations. The banners contained a claim that violated the Karnataka Prevention of Slaughter and Preservation of Cattle Act, 2020, which prohibits the slaughter of cattle but does not allow for the seizure of property as punishment.  Advocate Anshad Palya, State convener of the Federation of Muslim Organisations, criticized the banners as targeting a specific community and demanded clarification on the legality of the threat to seize property. The banners were later removed.

articles.title: Why Trump's Abraham Accords push is a non-starter - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump demanded that several Muslim countries join the Abraham Accords recognizing Israel, but experts believe this plan is unlikely to succeed.  Trump's announcement came during tense negotiations with Iran and amid pressure on a fragile ceasefire in the Middle East. The Abraham Accords, brokered by the US during Trump's first term, aim to build bridges between Israel and Arab countries. However, analysts argue that current political climate makes it unlikely for these nations to join given the ongoing war in Gaza and other factors.

articles.title: Trump-led push to redraw Congress maps faces setbacks in Southern states | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's push to redraw congressional district maps across the US to boost the Republican Party before the midterm elections has faced major setbacks in Alabama and South Carolina. A three-judge federal panel blocked Republicans in Alabama from moving forward with a new map that would eliminate one of the state’s two districts with major Black populations, while several Republican lawmakers in South Carolina joined with Democrats to shoot down a new map that would redraw a district held by Congressman James Clyburn. Both decisions are expected to be appealed to the US Supreme Court.

articles.title: Indian-origin woman killed at supermarket in Virginia; shooter had no connection with her, was later found dead - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 45-year-old Indian woman, Meghnaben Patel, was fatally shot at a convenience store in Virginia on May 23rd. Surveillance footage shows the attacker approaching the counter where she worked and shooting her multiple times before fleeing.  The shooter died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound after being found by police who were responding to reports of a domestic dispute that occurred earlier. Police have not identified any additional suspects in connection with the incident.

articles.title: Inquiry into Post Office Horizon scandal faces five-year delay without extra funding | Post Office Horizon scandal | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Metropolitan police are seeking additional funding and staff to continue their investigation into the Post Office Horizon IT scandal, which has been plagued by delays. Stephen Clayman, the commander in charge of the investigation, stated that a five-year delay is possible without the necessary resources, as they need nearly double the current team size to meet their deadline for submitting files to prosecutors. The investigation, codenamed Operation Olympos, aims to determine if perjury and perverting the course of justice occurred during the prosecution of over 900 post office operators between 1999 and 2015 due to faulty Horizon accounting software from Fujitsu.  The police are awaiting the publication of the second part of the inquiry's findings before moving forward with charging.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia turns to drones to shield pilgrims from extreme heat - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi health workers are utilizing drones to efficiently supply medical clinics treating heat-stressed pilgrims during the Hajj. The National Unified Procurement Company (NUPCO), responsible for logistics and supplies, has established a centralized operation center that manages drone deliveries of medications and other necessities. Drones have significantly reduced delivery times compared to traditional methods, ensuring faster access to critical supplies for patients.  This technological advancement is part of a larger effort to manage the Hajj's logistical challenges, including heat exhaustion, using AI-powered monitoring systems and traditional cooling measures like fans and mist systems.

articles.title: US picks potential partners for using Cold War-era plutonium as fuel | Nuclear Energy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Energy has selected five companies, including Oklo, to enter advanced talks about using surplus Cold War-era plutonium as fuel for nuclear reactors. The decision comes after the Trump administration announced plans to make approximately 20 metric tonnes of plutonium available to power companies.  Some lawmakers have raised concerns about weapon proliferation and economic sense of this plan, while others see it as a way to generate electricity and reduce nuclear liabilities.

articles.title: Four people killed after minibus collides with train in Belgium | Transport News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A minibus carrying nine people, including two children, collided with a high-speed train in Belgium near Buggenhout. The crash resulted in the deaths of the bus driver (49), an escort (27), and two children aged 12 and 15. Five children were injured and hospitalized in serious condition. Federal Police spokesperson An Berger stated that the minibus driver appeared to have driven through closed crossing barriers.  Prime Minister Bart De Wever expressed condolences for the victims' families, while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen offered her deepest sympathies.

articles.title: Tony Blair tells Starmer and rivals: abandon net zero and move closer to Trump | Labour | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tony Blair, a former Labour prime minister, has criticized current party leadership for abandoning the centre ground and jeopardizing the party's future.  Blair argues that the party should focus on policies like cracking down on welfare spending, removing restrictions on oil and gas, and repairing relations with Donald Trump. He also criticizes proposals from figures like Keir Starmer, Andy Burnham, and Wes Streeting for being impractical or lacking a clear vision. Blair believes these policies would strengthen the UK's position in the world and help Labour win the next election.  However, his views have been met with criticism from within the party who accuse him of abandoning social democratic values.

articles.title: Every migrant not tortured in home country: Trump tightens asylum rules, asks ICE to check frauds - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Donald Trump administration is ending the practice of fraudulent asylum claims by directing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to crack down on this alleged abuse.  ICE attorneys will now have greater authority to enforce the law, deterring false claims in immigration court. This directive follows a 2025 memorandum from President Trump highlighting how immigration attorneys frequently coach clients to conceal their pasts or lie about their circumstances when seeking asylum.

articles.title: Himachal panchayat polls: 78.53% polling in first phase, women voters outnumber men - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 78% of eligible voters participated in the first phase of Himachal Pradesh's panchayat elections, with women voters exceeding men in turnout. The highest voter participation was recorded in Kullu district at 84.43%, while Lahaul and Spiti had the lowest turnout at 69.40%.  The State Election Commission reported peaceful voting conditions across the state, with some minor issues such as a missing candidate's name on ballot papers leading to cancellations or postponements. The elections are being held in three phases, with results expected for various positions by May 31st.

articles.title: Iran supreme leader says regional nations will 'no longer be shields' for US bases - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, the Supreme Leader of Iran, declared that Middle Eastern nations would no longer serve as shields for US bases, asserting that the US's influence in the region is diminishing. He praised the Axis of Resistance, a network of Iranian proxies, for confronting American and Israeli influence and fighting the Islamic State group.  Khamenei also highlighted Iran's military successes against the US and Israel, while acknowledging ongoing indirect negotiations between Washington and Tehran focused on ceasefire stabilization and nuclear concessions. The conflict began with US-Israeli strikes on February 28th, which resulted in the assassination of Khamenei's father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

articles.title: Chemical tank rupture kills multiple people in US state of Washington | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A chemical tank rupture at a Nippon Dynawave Packaging facility in Longview, Washington, resulted in multiple fatalities and critical injuries. The incident occurred on Tuesday morning, causing the implosion of an 80,000-gallon tank containing white liquor, a chemical solution used in paper pulp production. Emergency responders transported at least nine workers and one firefighter to hospitals for treatment of burns and other injuries. Authorities confirmed fatalities but did not provide specific numbers.

articles.title: Rein in fossil fuel tax concessions, Labor MP says after BHP revelations | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: BHP and other mining giants are facing criticism for their slow progress on decarbonization, with Labor MP Jerome Laxale calling for more from the sector.  The Labor Environment Action Network (Lean) is pushing for changes to the diesel fuel tax credit scheme, arguing it should incentivize electrification instead of continued reliance on fossil fuels.  While some companies like Fortescue support the changes, others within the resources sector oppose them. The government has defended its current policy and stated that BHP is making progress but needs to accelerate efforts.

articles.title: Indians protest over ‘forever chemicals’ after relocation of scandal-hit Italian factory | Pfas | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Protests have erupted across India following an investigation revealing that an Italian factory shut down due to environmental contamination was acquired by the Indian company Laxmi Organic Industries and partially rebuilt.  Laxmi Organic Industries has denied allegations of pollution, but the relocation of equipment from Miteni, a former Italian plant linked to one of Europe's worst environmental scandals, has raised concerns about the transfer of polluting industrial practices from Europe to India. The investigation revealed that Laxmi included in its portfolio some of the same products once manufactured by Miteni and maintained commercial relationships with clients that previously sourced from the Italian company.  The issue has reached India’s parliament and environmental activists are calling for stricter regulations on Pfas, a group of "forever chemicals" known to cause cancer and other health problems.

articles.title: No Krishna Nagar in Lahore? Pakistan pauses heritage renaming plan after outrage by extremist elements - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan’s Punjab government has deferred its plan to restore the original historical names of roads and streets in Lahore following criticism from extremist groups. The decision comes after the Lahore Heritage Areas Revival (LAHR) committee, presided over by former Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif and current Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, initially approved the proposal.  The government now claims the matter is still under discussion, citing religious backlash as a reason for the retreat.

articles.title: Trump, near 80, to have annual physical amid scrutiny of recent ailments - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump, who will turn 80 next month, is scheduled to undergo his annual physical at Walter Reed National Military Medical Centre.  He has faced questions about his health following recent photographs showing a neck rash and swollen ankles. Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the president's health secretary, stated that Trump walks 14.5 kilometers every time he plays golf. Sean Barbabella, the White House physician, has attributed the neck rash to a common cream and said the president's cardiac age is approximately 14 years younger than his chronological age.

articles.title: US strikes Iran missile sites and mine laying vessels as Trump’s promised peace deal remains elusive | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US conducted airstrikes on southern Iran in a test of the seven-week ceasefire, targeting missile launch sites and boats attempting to lay mines.  Despite the strikes, Centcom stated that the action did not indicate an end to the ceasefire. While Iranian state media reported explosions near Bandar Abbas, Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, and central bank governor, Abdolnaser Hemmati, were among negotiators in Qatar, where talks are underway with the US on a potential deal.  Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaker of Iran’s parliament, led the delegation to Qatar. The US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, stated that a deal was still possible despite the strikes and emphasized the importance of reopening the Strait of Hormuz for global oil trade.

articles.title: Russia slams US for not granting visa to diplomat for UN meeting | United Nations News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Alimov was denied a visa to attend a United Nations Security Council meeting in New York, prompting Russia to accuse the United States of violating its obligations under the 1947 UN Headquarters Agreement.  Vassily Nebenzia, representing Russia, stated that granting visas is a requirement under the agreement and that denying Alimov's visa was disrespectful to both the Chinese presidency of the Security Council and an affront to international diplomacy. The US Department of State did not immediately respond to Al Jazeera's request for comment.

articles.title: Ireland to ban goods from Israeli settlements in West Bank by July - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Ireland aims to pass a law restricting goods trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank by mid-July. Helen McEntee, Ireland's Foreign Minister, stated that the legislation will impact only a handful of products, worth €200,000 annually.  Prime Minister Micheal Martin confirmed the bill will focus on goods and not services, citing impracticality and viability concerns. Business groups warned against expanding the ban to services, fearing it would harm foreign companies.  The move has drawn opposition from Israel, some US lawmakers, and international company lobbyists.

articles.title: Iran’s access to global internet starts to resume after 88-day blackout | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s internet access slowly resumed on Tuesday after an 88-day blackout, ending a period that caused widespread job losses and economic hardship. The resumption came despite questions about the authority of the body overseeing the move, called the “special headquarters for leading the country’s cyberspace.” While some internet service providers allowed limited connectivity, data from internet analysis companies indicated access was still less than 10% of pre-shutdown levels. Iranian officials acknowledged the gradual restoration process and cited concerns about economic damage caused by the blackout.

articles.title: White House proposes NDAs for all US federal workers | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The White House has proposed a guideline requiring all US federal workers to sign non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) to prevent unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information. The proposal, announced by the Office of Personnel Management, would allow the White House to take legal action against employees who violate the agreement and asserts that the government is entitled to royalties from disclosing such information.  The White House has faced criticism for its aggressive campaign against news outlets and media figures critical of it, including threats to revoke licenses of ABC stations and restricting reporters' access at the Pentagon.

articles.title: Israeli military dismisses former top lawyer from ranks over leaked 2024 video of Palestinian detainee's abuse - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s military dismissed its former top lawyer, Yifat Tomer-Yerushalmi, following a scandal involving a leaked video of soldiers abusing a Palestinian detainee. The case, which sparked international outrage and protests within Israel, led to Tomer-Yerushalmi's resignation last year.  The Chief of the General Staff, Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir, suspended her from service in light of the ongoing criminal proceedings. Katz hailed the dismissal as a step towards restoring trust in the military.

articles.title: Iran remains in peace talks despite first US strikes since ceasefire | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Despite US bombings of Iranian targets, a peace agreement between Iran and the US remained on the table. The Iranian foreign ministry denounced the attack as a violation of the ceasefire and threatened retaliation but did not withdraw from talks mediated by Pakistan and Qatar.  The conflict has escalated with Israel expanding its ground operations in Lebanon, prompting Khamenei, Iran's supreme leader, to call for unity among Muslim countries and predict the elimination of Israel by 2040. Brent oil futures climbed after news of renewed fighting.

articles.title: Gymkhana Club: Delhi's most exclusive club is under threat of shutdown - can it survive?
articles.rephrased_article: The federal government of India has ordered the closure of Delhi's Gymkhana Club by June 5th, citing the need for "defense infrastructure and other vital public security purposes". The club, which has long been a haven for retired generals, senior bureaucrats, and old business families, is challenging this order in court.  The government argues that it will not immediately take over the land but will only proceed with eviction after giving the club proper notice. This action follows years of scrutiny by Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government of elite institutions. The Gymkhana has been a symbol of inherited privilege and exclusivity, sparking debates about privilege, heritage, and public space in Delhi.

articles.title: Did Trump oversell a broken Iran ceasefire deal? | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump claimed a deal with Iran was "largely negotiated" but later stated talks were ongoing, sparking controversy over a draft US-Iran memorandum of understanding. The document has drawn criticism in Washington, alarm in Israel, and renewed questions about sanctions relief, nuclear talks, and the fragile ceasefire.

articles.title: More climate records under threat as spring heatwave bakes western Europe - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Western Europe experienced record-breaking temperatures on Tuesday, with France and Britain reporting the hottest May days on record. The heatwave, fueled by a "heat dome" from northern Africa, led to at least seven deaths in France, mostly due to drownings as people sought relief in water bodies.  The Met Office forecasted a drop later in the week but warned that such extreme temperatures are becoming more frequent due to climate change.

articles.title: French Open 2026 results: Naomi Osaka sparkles in golden 'Eiffel Tower' outfit in first-round win - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Naomi Osaka, the four-time Grand Slam champion, made a dazzling entrance at the French Open in a sparkling gold tennis dress designed by Nike. The outfit, inspired by the Eiffel Tower at night, drew praise from fellow players and fans alike.  Osaka's fashion choices have become a signature part of her Grand Slam appearances, with the recent outfit being no exception. Aryna Sabalenka, the top seed, expressed admiration for Osaka's confidence and self-expression on court.

articles.title: India’s energy strategy needs price correction - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Strait of Hormuz crisis has exposed the interconnectedness of energy security and geopolitics, impacting global crude markets and transportation costs. India, heavily reliant on imported oil, has implemented a combination of state intervention, supply diversification, and financial absorption to mitigate the impact on consumers. While petrol and diesel prices have remained relatively stable in India compared to other advanced economies, the country's reliance on fossil fuels remains a structural vulnerability. The government is facing pressure to implement a more sustainable approach to fuel pricing, balancing economic realities with consumer needs.

articles.title: EB-2 Green Card limit exhausted for India for 2026: What does it mean? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US State Department has announced that all available immigrant visas in the Employment-based Second Preference (EB-2) category for India have been issued for 2026.  Embassies and consulates may not issue EB-2 Green Cards for India until 2026, according to the department. The annual limit for EB-2 visas is 28.6 percent of the worldwide employment limit, with a cap of seven percent per country. This means that no further movement will occur in the EB-2 category until 2026.

articles.title: US Senate confirms veteran naval officer Frank Garcia as top Africa envoy | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Senate confirmed veteran naval officer Frank Garcia as Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, ending a vacancy that lasted over a year.  Garcia's nomination was approved by the full Senate after receiving support from several Democrats who had initially opposed it. Garcia, a former US Navy officer and intelligence consultant, advocates for a shift in US policy towards Africa, focusing on trade and investment rather than aid. He believes this approach aligns with core national interests and will be beneficial to both the United States and African nations.  His appointment fills a critical diplomatic role at a time of growing global competition for influence across the continent.

articles.title: Australia politics live: Quad countries ink deal to build surveillance network and Fiji port to counter China | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A new report from the National Tertiary Education Union (Nteu) reveals that university class sizes have increased significantly since pre-pandemic levels, with over 27% of tutorials now exceeding 30 students.  The report found that just 9% of tutorials meet optimal standards for student support, leading to concerns about compromised workloads and declining student outcomes. Dr Alison Barnes, president of the Nteu, stated that this "class size explosion" is impacting universities nationwide. The Quad group of countries – Australia, the United States, India, and Japan – announced a new initiative to strengthen critical mineral supply chains and build surveillance capabilities in response to China's growing influence in the region.  The Quad also pledged to invest $20 billion in these initiatives and connect South Pacific islands through undersea cables by year-end.

articles.title: Nasa unveils next steps to build permanent Moon base
articles.rephrased_article: NASA has unveiled plans for a lunar base, including robotic landers and hopping drones to be built by companies like Blue Origin, Intuitive Machines, and Astrobotic. The agency aims to have humans on the Moon before President Trump leaves office in 2028.  However, experts believe China is likely to be the first country to land humans on the lunar surface. Nasa's three-phase plan includes robotic exploration of the Moon's terrain and delivery of scientific instruments, followed by the construction of power facilities and semi-permanent housing for astronauts.

articles.title: Czech police release Russian bishop after ‘white powder’ found in his car | Czechia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Bishop Hilarion, a Russian Orthodox bishop, was released from detention in Czechia after being stopped by police on suspicion of drug possession. The Czech national drug headquarters received an anonymous tip-off alleging the transportation of narcotics and psychotropic substances.  Russia’s foreign ministry condemned the arrest as a politically motivated setup, calling it a “deliberate, orchestrated provocation”. The Russian Orthodox church described the incident as a "classic setup", while Czechia's chargé d’affaires in Moscow, Jan Ondřejka, was summoned to protest against the detention.

articles.title: Climate Minister Musadik Malik warns against water aggression, urges India to respect IWT - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Musadik Malik, Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination of Pakistan, warned against "water aggression" at the Fourth High-Level International Conference on the International Decade for Action “Water for Sustainable Development” in Dushanbe. He urged India to respect the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) and criticized India's unilateral suspension of its obligations under the treaty following an attack in Kashmir. Malik highlighted Pakistan’s vulnerability to water disputes and called for stronger international commitment to enforcing transboundary water agreements, emphasizing the need for regional cooperation on glacial melt and ecosystem preservation.
